summary: My slot was attention shape and KV/value-embedding cost. What worked: shrinking the short sliding window from 1024 to 512 tokens was a clean -0.0048 on the 2**18-batch base (c0c11f0, 0.998855, cell best at the time) and is a two-line change; and value embeddings on every layer instead of alternating gave my best number, 0.986010 on a1's depth-12 base (a38e795), though the gain over that base (0.986500) is within noise. What did not work: GQA (n_kv_head = n_head/2) cost +0.013, head_dim 64 instead of 128 cost +0.002, and - the most useful negative - none of the good changes stack. The window win was exactly zero once MLP_RATIO=6 made the block FLOP-heavier (+0.0002), and a5's per-channel resid/x0 lambdas, worth -0.0024 at depth 8, cost +0.0068 on my depth-12 model. Next I would stop stacking and instead re-tune the LRs (especially MATRIX_LR and EMBEDDING_LR) at the depth-12/wide-MLP operating point, since every architectural knob was moved far from where those LRs were tuned; and I would test the one clean cell I skipped, depth 12 with per-channel lambdas and the original alternating value embeddings.
